summary: Defines an RTCP Extended Report block for reporting packet delay variation metrics across a range of RTP applications. It is a standards-track specification.

eli5.summary: Voice and video packets should arrive evenly spaced. This memo adds a way to report how bumpy the arrival times were.

questions: rtcp xr packet delay variation block
how to report jitter in rtcp
what is rtcp xr packet delay variation
subtitle: A new RTCP report block that tells a sender how unevenly its packets arrived.

tldr.problem: Real-time audio and video are sensitive to packets arriving at uneven intervals, but RTCP had no standard block for reporting packet delay variation.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6798 defines an RTCP XR block (block type 15) that reports positive and negative delay thresholds with their percentiles, plus a mean, using either MAPDV2 or 2-point PDV.
tldr.outcome: Applications can use the numbers to size adaptive jitter buffers, and network managers can compare delay variation against targets such as a Service Level Agreement.

today: RFC 6798 is a Proposed Standard and the data shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It extends the RTCP XR framework of RFC 3611.

sections.title: What the Block Is For
sections.content:
RFC 6798 adds a new Extended Report (XR) block type to those in RFC 3611, for use with RTCP as defined in RFC 3550. The block reports packet delay variation (PDV) using one of two standard metrics: Mean Absolute Packet Delay Variation 2 (MAPDV2, from ITU-T G.1020) or 2-point PDV (from ITU-T Y.1540). These belong to the class of transport metrics in the RTP monitoring guidelines.

The metrics suit RTP applications that are sensitive to delay variation. Applications can use them to help adjust the size of adaptive jitter buffers. Network managers can compare actual delay variation to targets, such as a numerical objective or a Service Level Agreement.
sections.eli5: If a friend throws you balls at uneven times, it is hard to catch them. This report tells the thrower how uneven the throws felt.

sections.title: The PDV Metrics Block
sections.content:
The block is measured at the receiving end of the RTP stream. It refers to a source by SSRC and relies on the measurement interval in the Measurement Information Block of RFC 6776. It MUST be sent in the same compound RTCP packet as that block, and if the measurement interval is not received, the PDV block MUST be discarded.

The block is five 32-bit words long with a block length field of 4. The fields are:

  • BT (8 bits): the constant 15.
  • I (2 bits): whether values are sampled (01), interval (10) or cumulative (11). The value 00 is reserved, MUST NOT be used, and a block with it MUST be ignored.
  • pdvtyp (4 bits): 0 for MAPDV2, 1 for 2-point PDV.
  • Rsv (2 bits): set to zero and ignored by the receiver.
  • SSRC of source (32 bits).
  • Pos PDV Threshold/Peak and Neg PDV Threshold/Peak (16 bits each): delays in milliseconds, format S11:4. Positive means packets arrived later than expected, negative means earlier.
  • Pos PDV Percentile and Neg PDV Percentile (16 bits each): format 8:8, from 0 to 100.
  • Mean PDV (16 bits): the mean, in milliseconds, format S11:4.
  • Reserved (16 bits): MUST be zero when sent and ignored on receipt.
sections.eli5: The report is a small form with boxes for the biggest early and late arrivals, how often that happened, and the average.

sections.title: Number Formats and Special Values
sections.content:
The block uses binary fractions written as S X:Y, where S means two's complement signed, X is the number of bits before the binary point and Y the number after. So 8:8 is unsigned from 0.0 to 255.996, and S11:4 is the format of the three delay fields.

Special values signal problems in the delay fields. If a value is less than -2047.9375 (which would be coded as 0x8001), 0x8000 SHOULD be reported for over-range negative. If it is greater than +2047.8125 (0x7FFD), 0x7FFE SHOULD be reported for over-range positive. If the measurement is unavailable, 0x7FFF MUST be reported. For the percentile fields, unavailable is 0xFFFF.

When the type is 2-point PDV and both percentiles are 100.0, the two threshold values are the peak values measured during the reporting interval, and the difference between them gives the range of 2-point PDV.
sections.eli5: The numbers are packed into tiny boxes, with a few secret codes meaning too big, too small, or I could not measure it.

sections.title: Choosing a Metric Type
sections.content:
MAPDV2 is the envelope of instantaneous per-packet delay compared with the short-term moving average delay. It could be useful for judging residual impairment when an end system uses an adaptive de-jitter buffer that tracks the average delay variation, if its averaging behaves like the MAPDV2 algorithm.

2-point PDV reports absolute delay variation against a reference packet transfer delay, usually the packet with minimum delay. The two points are the sender, which applies RTP timestamps, and the receiver. The value for packet j is the quantity D(i,j) from RFC 3550. Because the metric includes clock frequency offsets in both end systems, it is mainly useful in networks where synchronization is distributed. It is likely to be useful with fixed de-jitter buffering, to size the buffer or to see whether existing buffers are now too small.

For 2-point PDV, the Mean PDV is the mean of per-packet values and compares the first media packet's arrival with the mean of all arrivals. A single value may not help, but an average over many sessions may help diagnose delay at session startup, for example media packets delayed behind signaling packets.
sections.eli5: There are two ways to measure bumpiness. One compares each packet to the recent average. The other compares each packet to the fastest one.

sections.title: Worked Examples
sections.content:
The RFC gives two examples. To report MAPDV2, set Pos PDV Threshold to 50.0, Pos PDV Percentile to 95.3, Neg PDV Threshold to 50.0 (implying -50 ms), Neg PDV Percentile to 98.4 and PDV type to 0. The average MAPDV2 is then reported in the Mean PDV field.

To report 2-point PDV, set Pos PDV Threshold to 60 (implying +60 ms), Pos PDV Percentile to 96.3, Neg PDV Threshold and Percentile to 0, and PDV type to 1. An implementation may fix the percentile and compute the matching level, or fix the threshold and compute the percentile. The RFC says the second approach is simpler, except for the 100th percentile.
sections.eli5: Example: tell me the delay that 95 out of 100 packets stayed under, and also the average.

sections.title: Signaling with SDP
sections.content:
XR blocks MAY be used without prior signaling. To signal use, the RFC adds a value to the rtcp-xr attribute from RFC 3611: pkt-dly-var, optionally followed by pdv= with the metric type, and threshold or percentile settings using nthr, npc, pthr and ppc.

In an offer/answer exchange, the sender of the SDP may request a specific PDV type and may give a threshold or percentile and expect the corresponding percentile or threshold back. The receiver SHOULD send the requested metrics, and if a metric is not available it MUST send the block with the flag value for unavailable.
sections.eli5: Before a call, one side can ask for this report and say which kind of measuring it wants.

sections.title: IANA and Security
sections.content:
IANA assigns block type 15 in the RTCP XR Block Type registry to the Packet Delay Variation Metrics Block, and registers the SDP parameter pkt-dly-var. A new sub-registry, "RTCP XR PDV block - PDV type", holds 4-bit values with 0 and 1 assigned as above and 2 to 15 reserved. New entries need Specification Required.

The RFC believes the block adds no new security considerations beyond those in RFC 3611. Since it carries no per-packet statistics, the confidentiality risk described in RFC 3611 does not apply.
sections.eli5: Reports like this do not give away much, so they add no new dangers to the ones already known.

fields.name: I
fields.desc: Sampled (01), interval (10) or cumulative (11); 00 is reserved.

fields.name: Pos PDV Threshold/Peak
fields.desc: Late-arrival threshold or peak in ms, S11:4.

fields.name: Pos PDV Percentile
fields.desc: Percentage of packets under the positive threshold, 8:8.

fields.name: Neg PDV Threshold/Peak
fields.desc: Early-arrival threshold or peak in ms, S11:4.

fields.name: Neg PDV Percentile
fields.desc: Percentage of packets beyond the negative threshold, 8:8.

fields.name: Mean PDV
fields.desc: Mean delay variation in ms, S11:4.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.desc: Zero when sent, ignored on receipt.
